question:
I am working on a PostgreSQL + dbt data platform where a mart table provides data for an API. Every time a row in the model is updated (incremental update) last_update timestamp should also be updated to communicate the API user that changes have been made.

However, this data needs to persistent so that when we do scheduled full refreshes, the last_update dates can be repopulated into the corresponding rows in the mart table from a persistent build ledger. Does someone have suggestions for an optimal pattern to implement this?

Options I've been considering

  1. Just use another dbt model (risking over-running rows with full-refresh)

  2. Post-hook (cumbersome logic)

Are these my only options? Or is there something I have overlooked here?
title: Creating a build ledger for a dbt model
answer:
There is only one good way to implement this requirement: a database row-level BEFORE trigger.

  • with a trigger, there is no danger that a bug in your application code forgets to set the timestamp

  • a trigger guarantees that the timestamp is always set in the same transaction as the data modification

  • a trigger will maintain the integrity of your data even if somebody modifies them manually (to "fix" some problem) or with a batch job that is not part of your application
